question: Does the source H473N product profile distinguish target accumulation from nondetection of a competing donor-route product, without isolating donor-half chemistry?
conclusion: In the same glycolaldehyde/pyruvate mixture, purified H473N accumulates less source-reported DHB than WT, while erythrulose is undetected. This is a product-specific endpoint contrast; it does not identify an elementary cause or a microscopic donor-specificity constant.

donor_half_assessment.question: Does Yu2020 directly distinguish pyruvate/cofactor donor-half chemistry from acceptor coupling in the same named construct?
donor_half_assessment.evidence: PDFp15 uses cross-acceptor final-yield correlation for H100L,H100F,H100Y and WT, four points total. PDFpp19-21 andp28 use drawn/MM2-minimized ThDP-enamine, modeled variants and sequential docking; the intermediate is supplied to the calculation.
donor_half_assessment.scope: No direct donor-only or donor-first adduct formation/occupancy/cleavage reporter is identified in the inspected main manuscript. Final product yields,apparent pyruvate KM and docking cannot assign a measured donor-half rate. The unacquired supplementary file and literature beyond this paper are not declared absent evidence.
donor_half_assessment.stopping_condition: Direct donor-half inquiry closed at its missing distinguishing endpoint; selected product-profile relation below is the supported alternative.

profile_context.assay_pair: The same supplied50mM glycolaldehyde/50mM sodium pyruvate mixture supports two source-depicted net routes. Glycolaldehyde is the acceptor in the target route and supplies both molecules in the competing erythrulose route.
profile_context.source_donor_origin_scope: Product structures and the source scheme associate DHB with pyruvate-derived transfer and erythrulose with the two-glycolaldehyde route. This is source chemical interpretation, not isotope tracing or a completed atom map. CO2 is depicted for the target route; no CO2 measurement is curated.
profile_context.target_contrast: WT10.5mM versusH473N5.5mM DHB are central values printed in Results. A shared query may compute the descriptive H473N/WT quotient; no second derived scalar is stored.
profile_context.competing_product_contrast: WT10.5mM erythrulose versus H473N source nondetection. No detection/quantitation threshold is stated. Do not compute its mutant/WT ratio or a DHB/erythrulose selectivity ratio.
profile_context.mechanistic_limit: A24h accumulated-product profile integrates both reaction halves,competition and possible reversibility/product release. It does not isolate pyruvate binding,decarboxylation,cofactor-adduct formation or a specificity constant. Equal accumulated concentrations do not determine microscopic fluxes or remaining substrate concentrations. The erythrulose route consumes two glycolaldehyde molecules per product; DHB uses one glycolaldehyde and one pyruvate.
profile_context.uncertainty_limit: Fig3C displays SD error bars from triplicates. Exact numeric SDs and underlying chromatographic/calibration data are unavailable in the inspected text and were not digitized; Fig3A itself is a displayed chromatogram. No propagated uncertainty,significance or equivalence claim.
profile_context.lysate_boundary: Fig3B is24h yield normalized by lysate TK densitometry, labeled specific activity by the source; it is not an initial rate and is not pooled with the purified Fig3C concentrations.
profile_context.source_naming_caution: The selected Results and Fig3C identify single H473N. Separate library methods print D473N/D473S and one propanal sentence prints H474S; those inconsistent strings do not redefine this selected single-mutant record. No exact sequence or broader library mapping is inferred.
